svg.title: One tools/call request and its three possible responses, annotated for debugging
svg.desc: A client box on the left sends one tools/call to a server box on the right. The request is printed underneath: five mirrored HTTP headers, then the JSON-RPC body with its params, arguments and metadata. Four numbered checks name what to read, in order. One, the MCP-Protocol-Version header must equal the protocol version in the metadata, because any difference is error minus thirty-two thousand and twenty, a header mismatch, answered with HTTP 400. Two, the client capabilities are re-sent on every request, so a missing elicitation key means a tool that asks a question gets minus thirty-two thousand and twenty-one. Three, the name header and every parameter header mirror a body field, and the server must verify each of them. Four, compare the arguments against the published input schema rather than against your Python signature, because the two differ. A second arrow runs back from server to client, labelled one of three responses, read resultType first and then isError. Three cards of identical size sit below it. The first is green and headed Success: resultType complete, content, structured content, isError false, HTTP 200, with a note to validate the structured content against the output schema before handing the content to the model. The second is red and headed Failure, nothing raises: the same resultType complete and the same HTTP 200, but the content holds an error message and isError is true, so the call returned normally and a client built on try and except believes it. The third is red and headed Failure, the client raises: a JSON-RPC error object with a numeric code and message and no result member at all, with a note that each cause carries its own code, minus thirty-two thousand six hundred and one for an unknown method and minus thirty-two thousand and twenty for a header mismatch. A closing line states the rule: an error object means the server could not act on the request at all, while isError true means the request was fine, the tool ran, and it failed; the first two are HTTP 200 and the third depends on the code.
svg.text: Reading a wire trace: one request, three responses
Two of the three responses are failures, and only one of them looks like one.
